"""
Lessons From Twitch, Ping, and T3
Theo traces his ability to adapt quickly to AI agents back to lessons learned across his career about balancing product work with platform infrastructure [15:42].

Finding system clarity at Twitch: After struggling on a legacy Go codebase on Twitch's VOD team, Theo moved to React and TypeScript just as React Hooks launched [07:21]. Hooks matched his functional programming background in Elixir, giving him a full mental model of how changes rippled through a system [07:37].

Product vs. Platform separation: Twitch divided engineering into user-facing product teams (like Chat, Creator Dashboard, and Mod Tools) that owned features end-to-end [09:30], and platform teams (like Browser Clients, GraphQL Edge, and core infrastructure) that kept repos scalable and unified [10:49].

"Fix the cause, not the symptom": Early at Twitch, Theo submitted a messy PR based on confusing docs and existing code [12:52]. Instead of simply rejecting it, senior engineer Derek immediately opened two PRs to fix the misleading docs and rewrite the bad examples in the repo [13:11]. That taught Theo that code quality is an organizational setup problem—making the right path easy raises the floor for everyone [15:58].

Bridging the divide: Theo used smaller internal tools (around 300 users) to dogfood ideas before proposing them to the main Twitch web platform team [14:09]. He also learned that painful technical workarounds often vanish with direct communication—such as resolving a debate over storing a nested dashboard layout by asking the GraphQL Edge lead directly, who immediately approved using a simple JSON blob instead of a complex flat node array [22:53].

The T3 Stack: Leaving Twitch to build Ping alone stripped away his dedicated platform teams [18:06]. After over-engineering early setups, he created the T3 Stack—combining Next.js, TypeScript, React, Tailwind, Prisma, and tRPC—so TypeScript itself acted as a low-friction contract across the stack [19:06]. While juggling company building and content creation, he split his coding roughly 50/50 between invisible platform improvements and visible product features [21:18].

His final manual overhaul: Before undergoing hand surgery, Theo spent a month migrating T3 Chat from a fragile custom sync engine to Convex in a 25,000+ line PR [27:11]. While users barely saw a direct difference beyond smoother multi-device syncing, the move unblocked teammates Julius and Mark so they could ship rapidly without depending on him [28:22].

Old slop blocks new models: Theo describes his old custom sync engine as "slop" that slowed his human team down, drawing a direct parallel to AI workflows: "Sonnet 4.5 slop was blocking Opus 5.5" [30:16].

Tooling is always malleable: From messaging TypeScript's Daniel Rosenwasser on Twitter at age 21 to help fix 15–20 minute type-check times at Twitch, to later building TS Rust and speaking with TypeScript's creator, Theo stresses that underlying developer tools can always be improved [31:04].

Becoming a Codebase "Gardener"
Instead of writing every line of code directly, an engineer's primary job is now tending the environment so AI agents grow code cleanly without letting clutter take over [32:49].

New engineering economics: Refactors that once demanded massive human coordination—like Twitch's month-long, 8-person Google Sheet effort to migrate from Apollo GraphQL v2 to v3—now take a single prompt [34:40]. Conversely, investing in custom developer tooling (like rewriting TypeScript in Rust for a 3-person team) is now worthwhile [33:50].

Friction hurts agents worse than humans: Five-minute dev-server startups block agents and burn prompt-cache TTLs and tokens [36:46]. Heavy CI resource usage bottlenecks parallel agent runs [37:03], and slow release pipelines discourage merging [37:15].

Slop multiplies fast: Left untended, AI-generated clutter—"weeds"—spreads through a repo much faster than human mess ever did [37:46].

Concrete Gardening Tactics and Results
Theo shares specific maintenance practices he uses on T3 Code and T3 Chat to keep agents productive:

Pruning 250,000 lines of useless tests: Theo deleted roughly half of all unit tests in T3 Code in a single PR because bloated tests caused AI agents to copy those patterns and generate even more pointless edge-case tests [38:33]. Only four out of roughly 11,000 deleted tests ever had to be restored, with zero missed regressions [39:04].

Root-cause thread tracing: When an unnecessary test still slips into a PR, the team asks the contributor to inspect the AI thread and ask the agent why it wrote that test, then updates repo guidance to eliminate the root trigger [39:33].

Adding CI "wooden stakes": To protect T3's wire-protocol efficiency (keeping large thread loads near 5 KB), Theo built an automated GitHub Action called the "thread transfer impact" tool that simulates real event data in under 45 seconds and flags payload regressions with red Xs [40:04]. This guides both reviewers and monitoring agents toward what matters [41:06].

Dramatic PR velocity gains: By continuously clearing friction and guiding agents, T3 Code grew from merging 2–20 PRs per day to 60 on slower weekend days and 400+ PRs per day on active days [43:21].

Theo wraps up by noting that fellow developer Lauren independently reached the exact same "gardener" metaphor for monitoring PR streams and trimming creeping lint suppressions and slop [43:48]. While the rapid pace of change can feel intimidating, embracing this platform-gardening mindset has made building software more enjoyable for him than ever [44:54].""""

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. # AGENTS.md

Moneo is an open-source personal-finance app you run on your own computer. One owner imports statements or syncs a bank, tracks accounts and wealth, plans spending, and asks about their money in chat, artifacts and voice calls.

Stack: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript. The backend is Postgres plus the open-source Supabase Auth, PostgREST and Storage services in Docker (`docker-compose.yml`). Drizzle schema, Workflow (local world) for durable jobs, Vitest and Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK, paid by the owner's ChatGPT plan or an API key.

These are defaults. The developer's instructions override them; if a rule conflicts with the task, say so and ask.

## Non-negotiables

- **Local-first.** Everything listens on `127.0.0.1`; optional phone access is Tailscale forwarding to it (`lib/phone-access.ts`). Data leaves the machine only for services the owner set up (AI provider, Enable Banking, Scalable). New features must work fully offline from the cloud except those calls.
- **One owner, no accounts.** The proxy signs the owner in automatically; there is no sign-up or sign-in screen. Private access from the owner's own Tailscale devices needs no login; anything public must add one first.
- **Financial truth comes from code and data, never from AI guesses.** Money is integer minor units (`bigint`) with an explicit currency. The AI explains and proposes; every write it suggests is a card the owner accepts.
- **History is kept.** Preserve source records, corrections, history and undo when changing financial data flows.
- **Open source.** No secrets, private statements or personal data in the repo (`npm run check:privacy` runs before tests and lint).

## How to work

1. **Think before coding.** State your assumptions. If a request has more than one reading, name them and ask instead of picking silently. If a simpler approach exists, say so.
2. **Simplicity first.** Write the least code that solves the problem: no speculative features, options or single-use abstractions. Prefer existing utilities and dependencies, and Zod for validating user and external input. Would a senior engineer call it overcomplicated? Then simplify.
3. **Surgical changes.** Touch only what the task needs and match the nearby style. Remove what your own change made unused; mention unrelated dead code instead of deleting it.
4. **Goal-driven.** Turn the task into checks you can run, then loop until they pass. A bug fix starts with a test that fails on the current code. Purely visual changes get a before/after screenshot instead.

## Safety

- Never run tests or experiments against the owner's workspace. Browser tests use the QA user (`scripts/e2e-auth.mjs`) or disposable users they create and remove.
- Never delete the Docker volumes (`docker compose down -v`) or drop the database: that is the owner's financial history.
- Never change `JWT_SECRET`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` or `BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in an existing `.env`; keys, sessions and stored bank and ChatGPT tokens stop working.
- Never commit `.env*` (except `.env.example`), `.data/`, `e2e/.auth.json` or `.qa/`.
- Only kill processes you started, or ones you verified by port and working directory. Never kill by name.
- Real AI, bank and Scalable calls cost money or count against limits (PSD2 allows about 4 background bank fetches a day). Mock them in tests unless the task is to check the real service.

## Hit every surface

Before calling a feature done, check where else it shows up:

- Pages and their mobile layout, light and dark.
- Chat tools and the system prompt in `lib/ai/provider.ts`, artifacts, and the voice call (`lib/ai/voice-*`).
- Home widgets and the command palette.
- Background jobs (`lib/scheduler.ts`, `workflows/`) and imports from files, banks and Scalable.
- The reverse path: undo, reset all data, reconnect, disconnect.
- Docs: `README.md` for anything the owner sets up or runs, `.env.example` for new variables. Deferred work goes in GitHub issues.

## Commands

Use npm (`package-lock.json` is authoritative).

- Install: `npm ci`
- Backend: `npm run setup` (writes `.env` secrets, starts Docker, applies migrations, creates the owner; safe to rerun)
- Dev: `npm run dev` (http://localhost:3000)
- Unit: `npm test` · Lint: `npm run lint` · Build: `npm run build`
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e` (see `e2e/README.md`)

## Project map

- `app/` — App Router pages, route handlers, server actions
- `lib/finance/` — deterministic financial logic
- `lib/ai/` — models, chat tools, ChatGPT sign-in (`chatgpt.ts`), voice
- `lib/bank/`, `lib/scalable/` — Enable Banking and Scalable Capital
- `lib/schema.ts` + `supabase/migrations/` — database schema
- `workflows/` — durable background jobs; `lib/scheduler.ts` runs the daily ones
- `docker-compose.yml`, `docker/`, `scripts/setup.mjs` — the self-hosted backend
- `e2e/` — Playwright flows; `supabase/tests/` — SQL regressions

## Sign-in callbacks and addresses

Each outside service sends the browser back to a different address. Keep these in mind before changing ports, hosts or remote access:

- **Sign in with ChatGPT** (`lib/ai/chatgpt.ts`): OpenAI only accepts the loopback `http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/api/ai/chatgpt/callback`, so sign-in happens on the computer running Moneo. Tokens are stored there, so chat works from any device afterwards.
- **Enable Banking** (`lib/bank/return-listener.ts`): production apps need an `https://` redirect registered in the Enable Banking app. Moneo uses `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` (a local listener with a cert from `npm run setup`), which forwards to `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`.
- **Scalable Capital** (`lib/scalable/server.ts`): dynamic client registration with `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL/api/scalable/callback`. `localhost` registers freely; other hosts need Scalable's allowlist (it rejects `*.ts.net`).
- **Supabase** (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `127.0.0.1:54321`): only the server may call it; never send the browser there, or it breaks on other devices.
- **Phone and tablet** (`*.ts.net` through Tailscale Serve): the laptop's addresses above never change. The three logins refuse to start from a remote device (`lib/remote-device.ts`) and say to use the computer; everything else, including sync, works from there.
- **Voice** needs a secure context (https or localhost) for the microphone.

## Database changes

Add a new ordered migration in `supabase/migrations/` and keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned. Never rewrite an applied migration. `npm run setup` applies pending ones and records them in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. For other Supabase CLI commands use `npx supabase ... --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL"` (from `.env`).

## Validation

Run the smallest relevant test while iterating. Before finishing, run `npm test` and `npm run lint`; add `npm run build` for app, config or build changes, and Playwright for changed user flows. Await real events in tests; don't add sleeps or polling.

## Commits and pull requests

- Break the work into steps and commit each one; a big task is several commits.
- Never open a pull request unless asked.
- Write commit messages in plain language: what changed and why.
- Deferred work gets their issue created on github.
- suggest edits in agents.md if there was something that is changed or needs to be there in agents.md but only suggest when it is actually needed dont suggest just for suggesting.(only for prs)

## Context

Read only what the task needs: `.env.example` for environment names, `e2e/README.md` for browser tests, `supabase/tests/README.md` for SQL checks.

- [Python edits need UTF-8](python-edits-need-utf8.md) — open() is cp1252 here; non-ASCII gets corrupted
- [AI keys for dev](qa-chat-needs-openrouter-model.md) — OpenRouter out of credits 2026-10-27; OpenAI key (gpt-live-1) in main and voice worktree .env since 2026-10-30
- [Cash balance default account](cash-balance-default-account.md) — stated cash goes to the currency's cash account; create or ask when none or several
- [Voice feature branch workflow](voice-feature-branch-workflow.md) — PRs go into t3/voice-finance-agent; user opens final PR to main; ignore Entire gate
- [Voice design decisions](voice-design-decisions.md) — GPT-Live hands off to /api/chat, parallel tasks without a limit, tap-only cards, one mic with Send/Done
- [Overnight autonomy and subagent models](overnight-autonomy-and-subagent-models.md) — decide with my recommendation and report later; subagents use Opus 5.5 low or Sonnet 5.5; test voice against the real API
- [Audit fix decisions](audit-fix-decisions.md) — forecast with coverage, proposal default account rules, privacy contact address
- [Perf measurement setup](perf-measurement-setup.md) — measure on a prod build with a seeded QA workspace; React cache() is a no-op in route handlers
- [UI feedback pass decisions](ui-feedback-pass-decisions.md) — no cash-flow in net worth, masonry home grid, Ask-only ledger search, hidden scrollbars
- [Self-hosted pivot](self-hosted-pivot.md) — open-source self-hosted via Docker; keep local Supabase pieces; ChatGPT sign-in and API key equal; phone access via private Tailscale
- [Scalable trading decisions](scalable-trading-decisions.md) — card-only buy/sell/cancel, no limit, previews only on real account
- [Artifact Scalable + sliders](artifact-scalable-and-slider-decisions.md) — snapshot default with Settings live toggle; Pages keep JS; card sliders rerun in browser QuickJS
